lesson: In GOAP-based AI systems, interrupt evaluation often triggers expensive plan computation that is only used for freely-interruptible actions. Guard plan computation behind interruptibility checks to avoid wasteful search.

When GOAP search consistently exhausts budget for specific goals, track them and skip re-search until the world changes in ways that could make the goal plannable (position, inventory, wounds). Needs-only changes rarely alter search space.

POSITION dirty bit aggressively clears the search_exhausted_goals cache during multi-leg travel. Tracking last_in_transit state and only clearing when the agent genuinely arrives (transit-to-settled transition) preserves the cache across waypoints, avoiding redundant GOAP searches.

For GOAP planners with budget-limited search, track goals that previously exhausted the budget. When the exhausted-goals cache is cleared (due to world changes), re-search these goals with a reduced budget (e.g., 50%) since they are likely to exhaust again. This preserves the ability to find plans while reducing wasted computation on chronically unsolvable goals.

Exponential backoff on GOAP search budget (halving per exhaustion, floor at 64) is more effective than a flat reduction. Chronically unsolvable goals get searched with minimal effort (87.5% reduction after 3 failures) while preserving plan-finding ability. Clear exhaustion counts when a plan IS found to reset the penalty.

When maintaining per-goal exhaustion counts for GOAP search budget backoff, clearing ALL counts on any plan success defeats the backoff for chronically unsolvable goals that share a planning tick with solvable ones. Only clear counts for goals that actually found plans.

GOAP search max_node_expansions was over-provisioned at 512. Reducing to 256 caused zero test failures across 2700+ tests while cutting worst-case search cost in half. Most plans are found within 50-100 expansions.

In GOAP candidate planning, if candidates are searched in priority order, the first found plan is always the best selection. Early termination after the first found plan skips all lower-priority searches.

TTL-based exhaustion skip (BTreeMap<GoalKey, Tick>) is save/load safe while indefinite accumulation (BTreeSet) breaks determinism. TTL prevents the alternating-tick re-search bug while ensuring periodic retry as conditions evolve.

Backoff floor of 16 expansions is the sweet spot for chronically unsolvable goals. 32 still costs 5-8ms; 16 costs ~3ms; 8 shows no measurable gain (fixed overhead dominates). 16 is sufficient to detect newly solvable goals while minimizing waste.

Goal-aware exhaustion invalidation (ExhaustionInvalidationCondition + ExhaustionBaseline) combined with exponential budget backoff (consecutive_budget_exhaustions counter, halving per failure) is the most effective GOAP perf pattern. The invalidation system ensures re-search only when relevant state changes; the backoff minimizes cost when re-search is triggered but goal is still unsolvable. Total campaign gain: 63% reduction in golden test wall time.

After heavy AI-budget optimization, the system dispatch (especially perception and combat) becomes the dominant per-tick cost. Always re-profile after a major optimization campaign — bottlenecks shift.

Functions that linearly scan the append-only event log (e.g., latest_wound_event) degrade as O(total_events_ever_emitted) per call per tick. In long-running scenarios (7200 ticks), this creates 2-7ms/tick cost that grows linearly. Bound all event log searches to a fixed window.

VisibilitySpec::Hidden does NOT mean invisible to perception. The steal action deliberately uses Hidden+SamePlace semantics so co-located agents CAN witness theft via Crime+Transfer event tags. Do not skip hidden events in the perception event loop.

Search budget backoff must apply to the expansion budget, not just cooldown timing. Halving max_node_expansions per consecutive failure (threshold 3+, floor 16) gives 24% improvement on expensive seeds. Prior code only backed off cooldown — the budget itself was always full.

CognitiveProfile parameters max_node_expansions (224) and snapshot_travel_horizon (6) are at functional minimums. 128 expansions breaks golden_knowledge_asymmetry tests, horizon 3 breaks multi-hop travel tests. Optimization must target per-expansion cost or planning frequency, not these caps.

Needs dirty detection cannot use band-based coarsening — even 5-permille bands break golden_merchant_selling. The golden test suite enforces exact-tick responsiveness to need changes. Use plan commitment margins (S74) instead of observation coarsening.

Soak performance optimizations are seed-sensitive. Needs-only plan continuation (top-2 check) causes 88% regression on seed 4 while improving seed 3 by 9%. Always verify across ALL seeds in the cycle before accepting.
